source: the ice near the lens that is drawn piece by piece: blocks with faces, each a true body on an orbit of its own, lit by the Sun, with a shadow on the sheet. Lengths in planet radii, a size is the radius of a block, angles in degrees. Read by blocks.ts.

fade.note: a block shows by its width on screen: gone under the first number of pixels, whole from the second, so far ice is the sand of the sheet and not dots. largest: a block that would pass the lens wider than this many pixels is not made. frames: how many frames before and after the skim the lens is followed when the blocks are chosen.

classes.note: per class: perArea, how many blocks of at least the smallest size lie on one square radius of a dense ring; size, smallest and largest; power, the number above a size falls with the size to this power; height, the scale of how far the orbit swings out of the sheet (0: the block rests in the sheet with its centre lift sizes above it); swing, the largest such height; bySheet, 1 if the class lies where the sheet is (by its depth over presence, also past the rim where it thins out), 0 if it lies everywhere between the two radii of span; stray, how far the orbit is from a circle; shadow, 1 if the class throws shadows on the sheet; reach, how far from the lens a block shows, in heights of the lens over the sheet: whole up to the first, gone from the second; follow, how far the brightness of a block is that of the sheet where it lies (1) or that of ice on a dense ring wherever it is (0).
name: resting
low
high

shape.note: one block of twenty faces whose corners are moved in and out by jitter; each block is squashed along two of its axes (smallest and largest share), turned about an axis of its own and tumbles at up to tumbleDegPerSecond.

light.note: level: the brightness of a face that lies flat over the brightness of the sheet. ref: the brightness in the ring model of the dense ring that a block has where it does not follow the sheet. wide: the sheet's brightness is read averaged over this many radii. direct: a face that looks at the Sun is brighter than a flat one by the angle, up to this factor. bounce: the light a face gets from the lit sheet below it; sky: the share of that for a face that looks up. through: light that passes through the block to a face turned from the Sun. gloss and glossPower: the mirror flash of a face. white: the share of clean white ice in a block, smallest and largest, the rest is ice of the colour of the sheet there. tone: how far the brightness differs from block to block. ice: the colour of clean ice.

shadow.note: the shadow of a block on the sheet: a soft ellipse along the Sun's azimuth, as long as the Sun is low. strength: how much of the sheet's light it takes where the sheet is dense; soft: the share of its half width over which its edge fades (no less than softPixels pixels); height: a block this many sizes above the sheet throws a shadow of half the strength.
